title: Adaptive Planning
hook: The plan you wrote in January has no idea what happened in March.
statement: Plan in a way that adjusts as you go. Keep the destination, update the route.
explainer: Markets shift, customers surprise you, things break. A plan that never changes after missed targets isn't discipline. It's ignoring the data.
sop: Set yearly goals that name the destination, not every step.
Break the work into monthly or quarterly cycles.
At the end of each cycle, compare actual results to the plan.
Update next cycle's Plan using that Feedback, not your old assumptions.
Only change the destination if the data says it was wrong.
equation_example: This quarter's plan is 100. Results came in short, so the Feedback adjustment is -10. 100 - 10 = 90 for next quarter. A plan that keeps moving toward reality is working. One that never changes isn't listening.
question: Write down one part of your current plan you're following just because it's written down.
closing_statement: Hold the destination firmly and the route loosely.
caption:
Principle Nº 199: Adaptive Planning
